browser: The user's stable Google Chrome, driven through the official Claude in Chrome extension in its own tab-group window. Keys were synthetic in-page keydown/keyup events; touch buttons were pointer events on the real touch buttons; Start, language, board tiles and Play again were real mouse clicks. Only visible DOM text and canvas pixels were read; no game state was read or injected.
phoneLayouts: Checked in a same-origin 390-wide portrait frame on the page.
servedSourceCheck: The SHA-256 of all four served circuit-weaver modules was computed in the page and matched 32215f3e, 8270a5ad, 2df0a6b6 and 509354aa.

observed: A driver that reads only the status-line prompt, with a 0.2 s reaction delay, played boards 1 to 24 in English back to back in under 5 minutes and reached 'Nicely played! Every board is wired and humming!' with the maximum score of 3840 and no fuse blown. On one board the optimal route passed briefly through a 3 V + 9 V short, which the banner reported before the next turn cleared it.
Chinese board select listed all 24 boards.

Chinese: spending the 18-turn budget of board 10 three times blew the three fuses and ended the run with '三根保险丝都烧断了，再试一次！'; arrows, Space, Z and X on the loss screen changed nothing, and Play again returned to board select.

Chinese phone frame, 371 px wide with no horizontal overflow: the touch arrows and Turn button selected board 1, and touch taps alone following the prompt cleared boards 1 to 3. On board 4 the Undo touch button reverted a turn and Inspect showed the network line on the canvas.

At 390 px the English header read 'Open ends: 4 · Press Space to turn t…', keeping the verb and key visible after the tip; during the first seconds of a board the tip pushes the prompt out of the clipped header while the canvas footer still shows it.

limitations: Physical phones, other browsers, tapping tiles on the canvas and audio were not tested; console output was not captured.
